text:
lee: Quick check: I'm prototyping "resume beacons" (lightweight progress beacons) for long streaming responses. Aim: let the edge create a resumable checkpoint so retries only fetch the delta. Thoughts?
samir: Sounds promising. How are beacons different than the pulses we've discussed?
claire: And transport-wise — can we avoid changing gRPC wire semantics too much?
lee: Beacon = tiny signed blob (seq, visible_offset, epoch, hmac). Emitted inline periodically (client opt-in). Unlike earlier "pulses" ideas, beacon also carries a compact prefix-hash that lets some stateless runtimes validate resume without holding large state.
jordy: Prefix-hash? Explain quickly.
lee: Model runtime computes a rolling hash over the prefix tokens (deterministic transform). Beacon includes that hash so when gateway asks to resume at seq X, runtime checks hash matches and, if so, can stream only suffix. If mismatch, runtime rejects resume. This reduces need for heavy checkpoint storage.
samir: Neat. But risk: hash collision or intentional spoofing?
claire: Also, how do clients avoid duplicate-visible tokens on partial resumes?
lee: Mitigations: 1) use cryptographic HMAC over (stream-id, seq, prefix-hash, expiry) signed by runtime key; gateway verifies. 2) Gateway dedup stream-side: it keeps last-emitted-seq and drops tokens with seq <= last_emitted. The contract expects monotonic seqs.
jordy: Where does the rolling hash live? Model runtime or a shim? Some open model binaries can't easily add that.
lee: We add a thin shim in the serving runtime that can compute the rolling digest cheaply (streaming, incremental). For runtimes that can't support it, beacon resume is unsupported and gateway falls back to hedging. We'll mark models as resume-capable in the catalog.
samir: What about state at the gateway? Even if token is small, 100k concurrent streams is nontrivial.
lee: Gateway stores only last_emitted_seq + last_beacon_token per stream (~few hundred bytes). Default eviction 20s idle. Plus a global soft-limit that flips gateway into best-effort no-resume mode (fail-open) if streams > threshold.
claire: Billing: Do beacons count as billable tokens or requests?
lee: Beacons are metadata — not billed. If resume succeeds, only delta tokens are billed; if resume fails and we full-retry, model tokens for the full run are billed per normal. We'll add quota on resume attempts to limit abuse.
jordy: UX: clients opt-in? Backwards compat?
lee: Opt-in header `X-Resume-Beacon: 1`. Gateway advertises resume capability to clients via handshake. No header = unchanged behaviour.
samir: Transport: gRPC needs a control frame or multiplexed envelope. HTTP chunked can carry a beacon preface. We should include canonical wire examples in the RFC.
claire: Observability: we need resume_attempt, resume_accept, resume_reject_reason, dedup_drops, resume_latency. Also record which models reject resume due to missing digest support.
lee: Agreed. And add a sampling of full-token-diffs for debugging duplicates.
samir: Security: make tokens TTL-limited and rotate runtime signing keys. Also rate-limit resume attempts per client/IP.
jordy: Failure modes: if resume accepted but suffix conflicts with client expectations (e.g., deterministic vs sampling differences), we might still produce slightly different suffix. How to handle?
lee: We treat resume as "best-effort" — contract states that if runtime verifies prefix-hash, it promises deterministic continuation under the same sampling parameters. For non-deterministic settings we mark model non-resumable. We'll also default to conservative sampling (seeded) for resumable-serving path.
claire: Perf sims needed: pick RTTs 250/500/750ms, model-chunk 400/800ms, and concurrency up to 50k. Tune beacon interval and idle eviction. I'll run sims.
samir: Also simulate adversarial clients that spam resume attempts to inflate cost. Add per-stream and per-tenant caps.
lee: Prototype plan: 1) implement beacon emission in gateway shim, 2) add simple digest in dedicated runtime shim, 3) wire resume API (`POST /resume { token, seq }` streaming response of suffix), 4) enable behind feature-flag in staging.
deploy-bot: canary: resume-beacon feature flagged on staging (gateway-canary-2024-10-02) :white_check_mark:
jordy: One more: we should define clear fallbacks in router policy: resume_prefer | resume_safe | resume_disabled. Document tradeoffs.
lee: Yup. I'll update the RFC with protocol appendix, router policy, perf sims, and telemetry plan. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
